decision.headline: A real A/B test of these two posts is affordable: 117 people per version.
reasons: The simulated gap is 17.4 points (A 73.9% vs B 56.5%), inside a ±19.1-point interval: no winner.
A real test needs about 117 people per version to detect a gap that small (5% two-sided, 80% power): 234 in all.
There are about 23,020 Instagram users in Short North, Columbus, OH 43201 (Census x Pew join), so that test would have to reach 1.0% of them.
A test using at most 20.0% of the local audience (2,302 per version) can only detect a gap of about 3.5 points, so the next version must move intent by at least that much to be worth testing.

plan.success_metric: Taps through to the post and store visits attributed to the post (the real-world counterpart of the simulated intent to visit).
plan.decision_rule: Pick the version whose tap rate is higher by at least 3.5 points with a 95% interval that excludes zero; otherwise keep A and stop testing.
plan.stop_rule: Stop when each version has reached 117 people, or after 7 days.
assumptions: The real gap is no larger than the simulated one (simulated people, local Nemotron 3 Nano 4B; the backtest shows the crowd does not predict real winners).
A test is worth paying for only if it needs at most 20.0% of local Instagram users.
Audience size is an estimate: ACS adults in the ZIP times national Pew Instagram use by age.
